knowledge_type_note: A method rather than a tactic; it is kept separate from pawn-breakthrough, which is the sacrificial motif for forcing a passer.
engine_era_note: Engines time breaks far better than humans and are notably readier to delay one; the timing question the concept is about is exactly where they are strongest.

preconditions: A pawn advances into contact with an enemy pawn
indicators_for: Pieces already placed on the lines the break will open
The opponent must answer, committing their structure
A file or diagonal opens towards a target
indicators_against: The opponent is better developed and will use the opened lines first
The break opens a line towards your own king
Nothing of yours is placed to use what opens
recognition.detector: a pawn move that attacks an enemy pawn, from lib/features.js and the move generator
false_positive_traps: Any pawn advance into contact is mechanically a break; whether it is a good one depends on who is placed to use the lines it opens, which the detector cannot see.
A break is not a pawn-breakthrough. This base keeps them separate: the breakthrough sacrifices to force a passer, the break challenges a structure.
The break's value is often as an unplayed THREAT, and a position where it is available but not played may be the concept working correctly.

typical_plans: Place the pieces on the lines the break will open, then break
Break to force the opponent's structure to commit
Hold the break in reserve as a standing threat
typical_moves: c4-c5 and d4-d5 in queen's pawn structures
f4-f5 and e4-e5 against a king's position
...c5 and ...f5 as the standard freeing breaks for Black
typical_pawn_structures: Any fixed structure — the break is how a fixed structure stops being fixed
typical_piece_arrangements: Rooks behind the pawn that is about to advance
tactical_consequences: The moment of the break is usually the sharpest moment of the game
strategic_consequences: Whoever chooses the moment of the break usually chooses the resulting structure

exceptions: A break that opens lines for a better-developed opponent helps them.
Some positions are won by NOT breaking — keeping the tension is itself a plan, and the threat can be worth more than the move.
limitations: Detecting a pawn advancing into contact is mechanical; judging whether it is right is not, and this record does not claim the detector does.
This base holds one master-game example and no counterexample of a break played too early.
misconceptions: That a break wins material. It changes the structure and opens lines; material is a separate question.
That you should break as soon as it is available. The threat is often worth more than the execution.
That a break and a breakthrough are the same thing.

conflicts.resolution: Opposite methods against a structure and both correct at different moments: restraint keeps the opponent's pawns where they are, a break forces them to move. The question is which side benefits from the structure changing, and the answer is usually whoever is better placed for the lines that open.

examples.note: b5-b6 advances into contact with the black c7 pawn: the pawn now attacks c7 and can be taken by it, which is the contact this record defines a break as.

counterexamples.note: The same pawn one rank earlier making the same advance. b4-b5 arrives on a square where it touches nothing - c7 is still two ranks away - so it is a pawn move and not a break. The record's own note is that any advance into contact is mechanically a break; this is what happens one rank short of it.

by_level.beginner: A pawn move that runs into an enemy pawn, so the structure has to change and lines open up.
by_level.intermediate: A pawn break. Get your pieces onto the lines it will open BEFORE you play it.
by_level.advanced: It is often played to make the OPPONENT commit rather than to gain anything directly.
by_level.master: The break's value is frequently as an unplayed threat; timing it is the whole skill.

by_depth.short: A pawn advance that forces the structure to change.
by_depth.normal: A pawn break: an advance into contact with an enemy pawn, played to open a file or a diagonal for the pieces behind it, or to force the opponent's structure to commit. It is not played to win a pawn.
by_depth.deep: Pawn structures are stable because pawns cannot retreat, so a structure changes only when a pawn advances into contact — and whoever chooses when that happens usually chooses the terms. The break opens lines for both sides, so it favours whoever is better placed to use them, which is why breaking against a better-developed opponent is the standard misapplication. Its other and less obvious use is to force the opponent to commit: Fischer's 20.e4 against Spassky in 1972 was played not to gain material but to make one of two hanging pawns advance, so that the square it left could be occupied.

explanations.lesson: Put the pieces where the lines will open before you open them.

beginner_words: a pawn move that opens things up
avoid: break as soon as you can

definition_short: A pawn advance that challenges an enemy pawn, forcing the structure to change and opening lines the pieces behind it want.
definition_long:
The move that turns a static position into a decided one. Pawn structures are stable because pawns cannot retreat, so a structure only changes when a pawn advances into contact — and whoever chooses WHEN that happens usually chooses the terms.

IT IS NOT PLAYED TO WIN A PAWN. A break is played to open a file for the rooks, a diagonal for a bishop, or a square for a knight; or, in its other and less obvious use, to force the OPPONENT to commit — Fischer's 20.e4 against Spassky in 1972 is the model, played not to gain material but to make one of two hanging pawns advance so that the square it left could be occupied.

THE PIECES COME FIRST. A break opens lines for both sides, so it favours whoever is better placed to use them. Breaking while the opponent is better developed opens the position for them, which is the standard way the idea is misapplied.

TIMING IS THE WHOLE SKILL. The break exists as a threat before it is played, and the threat is often worth more than the execution — the opponent must keep guarding against it, which is a restraint on their own plans.

DISTINGUISH IT FROM A BREAKTHROUGH. A pawn BREAK challenges a structure and usually costs nothing; a pawn BREAKTHROUGH sacrifices material to force a passer past the defenders. This base keeps them as separate records because the second is a tactic with a calculation attached and the first is a strategic decision.
